thesis: Trust may legitimately be required to acquire religious understanding. However, when participant histories are offered as additional evidence that a practice reliably produces understanding, continued assent alone cannot determine which histories count. The strongest version is claim-relative: eligibility, completion, present exercise, and durable learning concern different outcomes, so an exclusion justified for one claim need not be justified for another. Retaining a history neither endorses its interpretation nor establishes that the practice failed.
claimed_contribution: The manuscript explicitly credits the elementary selection argument to Nguyen and the rejection of categorical dismissal of former members to Kent. Its proposed contribution is a framework connecting those points to legitimate religious apprenticeship: distinguish access from retrospective vindication, specify the transition being evaluated, justify exclusions without relying entirely on the agreement they produce, and preserve uncertainty about disputed qualifications.

findings.manuscript_location: §5, “A departure with a real qualification problem”: “The needed further evidence is consequently specific” and “what practical adjustments were available”; also the opening reference to “adherence to the taught technique.”
findings.claim: The case analysis omits available testimony bearing directly on accommodation and compliance.
findings.analysis: The manuscript correctly treats the account as uncorroborated testimony. Nevertheless, the cited account reports that a chair was provided and tried, with continuing discomfort, and that the participant introduced body scanning while breath-only practice was prescribed. These appear in the chair paragraph and the preceding discussion of his third day. The first supplies partial evidence about an adjustment actually attempted; the second supplies a possible qualification objection independent of his eventual dissent. The omission is demonstrated; neither reported fact establishes disqualification or failure. See [Hovhannisyan’s account](https://vahehovhannisyan.com/i-left-vipassana-on-day-five), paragraphs represented by lines 39–47 in the opened text.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: The general principle survives. The empirical illustration should narrow its description of what is unknown: accommodation is partly described in the existing testimony, and compliance presents an additional unresolved issue.
findings.repair_conditions: Include both reported details, distinguish their availability from independent corroboration, and assess whether the exercise modification matters to manageability, mastery, or neither. Do not convert either detail into a conclusive exclusion.

findings.manuscript_location: §3, “Which claim, which participants?”: “The proposed principle is consequently claim-relative”; §4, “What must be retained?”: “What matters is the local dependence of the argument”; §7, “Transformation and direct encounter”: “not silently convert failure under an earlier claim into confirmation of that claim.”
findings.claim: The literature positioning does not cover several close antecedents of the proposed refinement.
findings.analysis: V10 acknowledges its broad selection premise, so that premise is not an unacknowledged discovery claim. But the refinement also has substantive neighbors. [Christensen](https://quod.lib.umich.edu/cgi/p/pod/dod-idx/disagreement-question-begging-and-epistemic-self-criticism.pdf?c=phimp%3Bidno%3D3521354.0011.006%3Bformat%3Dpdf), pp. 1–2 and 18, restricts question-begging assessments of dissenters’ credentials. [ICH E9(R1)](https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/E9-R1_Step4_Guideline_2019_1203.pdf), §§A.3.2–A.5.1, makes outcome relevance depend on the specified question and distinguishes discontinuation from missing relevant evidence. [Riebel](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258191349_Self-Sealing_Doctrines_the_Misuse_of_Power_and_Recovered_Memory), pp. 40 and 43, discusses protecting practices by attributing failure to insufficient faith or incorrect performance. [Stilwell](https://philarchive.org/archive/STIWQM), pp. 6 and 10–12, addresses retrospective weakening of religious promises and faith-deficiency explanations. These overlap different components; none of the passages inspected supplies V10’s complete combination.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: The argument need not fail. Its defensible contribution is a synthesis and targeted application, with distinctions among entrant, completer, and current-practitioner claims, rather than a new general principle against circular exclusion or retrospective qualification.
findings.repair_conditions: Position the account against these specific arguments, explaining where its weaker local independence requirement, historical inclusion rule, and treatment of uncertain qualifications add something. Establish no claim of borrowing or chronological priority from resemblance alone.

surviving_contribution: A distinct remainder survives within this search: the manuscript organizes established concerns into a limited test for additional authority claimed from religious participation. Its most specific work distinguishes beginning a discipline, completing it, exercising a capacity now, and retaining understanding over time; separates historical inclusion from testimonial credibility and interpretive authority; and explains why a partly supported qualification objection can defeat a decisive criticism without establishing a clean success record. This is an application and synthesis with conceptual refinements. I did not establish that this exact combination is unprecedented.
remaining_questions: §4 says exclusion criteria may be internal to a tradition if their support does not derive entirely from filtered convergence. How much independence is required? A comparison with Christensen’s stronger dispute-independence requirement would clarify the boundary without requiring a religiously neutral competence test.

§6 permits committed participation while restricting subsequent corroboration. Buchak’s later “Faith and traditions,” §5, also discusses benefits of selective attention to agreeing sources. Does V10’s distinction adequately separate that permission from a community’s claim to additional evidential authority? This is a relevant neighboring challenge, not a demonstrated contradiction. See [Buchak 2023](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/nous.12427).

§5 expressly says it does not document an organization excluding this testimony from a success count. Consequently, whether an actual institution makes the criticized inference remains unanswered; the case establishes an analytical application, not its prevalence.

The frozen manuscript supplies no composition date. Public availability of the 2026 Stilwell preprint can be checked, but its chronological relationship to the development of V10 cannot be established from the permitted evidence.
limitations: This was a finite, primarily English-language public-web search conducted on 31 October 2026. Search results establish neither exhaustive originality nor the absence of closer predecessors.

All substantive comparisons below use opened primary texts. Locations_read identifies the portions inspected; availability of a complete source does not mean every page was read. The supplied manuscript and its entire bibliography were read.

Cohen’s article was accessible only as publisher metadata and references. Frangakis and Rubin were accessible only through their publisher abstract and metadata. Neither was treated as a fully examined argumentative predecessor.

Several direct requests failed initially. Search-result opening subsequently provided Buchak’s repository manuscript, Christensen’s paper, and Stilwell’s preprint. These are retrieved public texts, not independently authenticated archival copies.

The current Dhamma pages were checked. Their wording at the particular 2024 Armenian course, the manuscript’s stated access on 17 October 2026, and individual entry assessments were not independently established.
Hovhannisyan’s attendance, health, accommodations, and conversations remain reported events rather than independently corroborated facts. No medical judgment about eligibility or causation was made.

Kent’s and Riebel’s arguments were inspected without independently verifying their historical case narratives. Riebel’s quotation attributed to Watzlawick was not checked against Watzlawick’s original text and is not used to establish that earlier source’s argument.

The public Stilwell record lists May and August 2026 versions. The unversioned retrieved text was compared, but textual identity across those versions was not checked. No inference about V10’s authorship, influence, or borrowing follows.

Alston’s cited précis was checked; his full book was not. Buchak’s substantive section citations were checked, but the bibliography’s ancillary statement about differing final-page pagination across publisher and reprint versions was not fully verified.

closest_predecessors.overlap: Agreement guaranteed by selecting agreers cannot supply ordinary additional corroboration. This directly anticipates §2’s stipulated unanimity example.
closest_predecessors.difference: Nguyen’s selected network does not require V10’s distinctions among entering, completing, and currently exercising an acquired capacity.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: Application to legitimate apprenticeship and different claims about its results.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Author manuscript pp. 7–8, Paleo example and footnote 4; V10 §3 explicitly calls its elementary argument “an application of that point.”

closest_predecessors.overlap: Discounting a dissenter’s competence must avoid using the disputed conclusion to dismiss the dissent.
closest_predecessors.difference: Christensen’s independence principle governs credence revision and brackets disputed reasoning more broadly. V10 restricts a particular institutional inference and permits unequal weight and tradition-internal criteria.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: The weaker local restriction and preservation of historical trajectories across different evaluative purposes.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Christensen pp. 1–2 and §7b, p. 18; V10 §4, “the local dependence of the argument.”

closest_predecessors.overlap: The specified question determines whether post-discontinuation observations are relevant; success while participating does not by itself characterize the broader offered intervention.
closest_predecessors.difference: ICH addresses comparative clinical effects and statistical estimation. V10 addresses testimonial authority without requiring numerical estimation or randomized comparison.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: A philosophical application to faith-dependent competence, disputed interpretation, and incomplete qualification evidence.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: ICH §§A.3.2–A.3.4, A.4, and A.5.1; V10 §3, “The appropriate record depends on the claim for which it is offered.”

closest_predecessors.overlap: A practice can protect itself by explaining failure as insufficient commitment or incorrect participation.
closest_predecessors.difference: Riebel diagnoses self-sealing doctrines across religious and therapeutic settings. The inspected passages do not develop V10’s claim-relative permissions for legitimate exclusion.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: Distinguishing supported qualification objections from circular or excessive exclusions.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Riebel p. 40 and “Harming and Healing,” p. 43; V10 §4, “a properly formed participant would affirm.”

closest_predecessors.overlap: Religious promises should not retain their original evidential authority after failures are neutralized by changing their content or blaming deficient faith.
closest_predecessors.difference: Stilwell focuses on petitionary prayer, scriptural expectations, and reinterpretation. V10 focuses on who enters a practice’s evidential record and separates access, completion, and current exercise.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: The participant-history framework and preservation of disputed classifications. Priority relative to V10’s composition remains unknown.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Stilwell p. 6 and pp. 10–12; V10 §3, “the disappointing outcomes remain results of the earlier promise.”

closest_predecessors.overlap: Former-member testimony should be checked rather than rejected categorically.
closest_predecessors.difference: Kent concerns research credibility and corroboration, rather than the particular inference from participant outcomes to a practice’s reliability.

closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Kent conclusion, pp. 15–16; V10 §4 expressly acknowledges this predecessor.
